newsitem.title: USA: BUYSIDE FOCUS -- Puerto Rico $540 mln deal on deck.
newsitem.headline: BUYSIDE FOCUS -- Puerto Rico $540 mln deal on deck.

text.p: Thin supply and Puerto Rico's triple-tax free appeal should spur demand for Wednesday's $540 million Public Buildings Authority offering, but buyers appear to be keeping one eye on municipals' tight ratios to U.S. Treasuries.
Tom Moles, a managing director at J&W Seligman, said pricing will decide whether he buys the deal.
"It's probably going to be rich as hell just because of the supply in the marketplace," he said. "There is nothing around."
Talk Tuesday afternoon had the uninsured 2021 maturity coming at a 5.67 percent yield, while the AMBAC-insured 2027 maturity was expected to yield 5.52 percent.

Because interest on Puerto Rico debt is exempt from federal, state and local taxes, it is popular with investors in high-tax states such as New York and California, which place an income tax on out-of-state bonds.
"It's a great name for funds," Moles said. "They can move it around amongst the funds."
A municipal analyst said if Tuesday's new deals are any indication, Puerto Rico's deal should price at fairly strong levels.
"I think if I were a risk commitment guy at the moment I'd lighten up into this if I could," the analyst said. "I'd lighten up, I don't think I'd bail out."
Munis are at "really strong levels" relative to Treasuries, especially on the long end, the analyst said.
"Our market is doubly vulnerable," he said, explaining that munis are vulnerable not only to potential Treasury market weakness, but also because of their rich ratios versus governments.
Reid Smith, a principal and senior portfolio manager at Vanguard Group, said while he believes municipals remain fairly valued, they are leaning toward the rich end of their valuation.

"We are right at the cusp, but I don't necessarily think that it's a sell because I think given munis' supply going forward and the tremendous demand that we are going to have going into the normal July 1 coupon, I think the ratios should hold where they are now," Smith said. "But I would not be adding additional risk exposure posture or duration exposure in the municipal market right now."
Smith sees no credit red flags as far as Puerto Rico is concerned, he said.
"We think that they have stabilized from our perspective, and we think that they are okay," he said.

Chris Mier, a senior vice president and portfolio manager at Kemper Mutual Funds, said while he will take a look at the offering just as he would any large deal, price and other considerations such as call features and couponing will determine whether he is a buyer.
Mier agreed that supply has been light and munis have gotten a bit rich to Treasuries, but demand has not been overwhelming and the new issue calendar appears to be building.
"There is evidence that there is a slight build-up in the calendar, and that there is a little more refunding activity," he said. "I'm not finding it excessively hard to find what I need."
